_dating_note: One 'taken' date used to head this file and had gone stale: it dated the 2026-08-07 structural walk while arcs and clusters were being rewritten on 2026-08-08. The file is two things and now says so. structural_snapshot_taken dates the static halves — state_carriers, state_initialization, decision_boundaries — which are re-derived only by a fresh walk of the code. ledger_updated dates the living halves — signal_flows and path_ledger — which change with every cluster closed; each arc carries its own dated evidence, so this field is a freshness hint, not a source of truth.

PARTIAL arcs are counted and listed, never absorbed.
_status_vocabulary._owner_definition: owner = the mechanism that answers for the state's lifecycle and semantics: creation, mutation, invalidation, end of life (mandate items 5-6). ATTACHMENT — which object physically holds the field — is provable separately (a creation site, an instance lifetime) and does NOT by itself establish ownership; nor does absence of traffic DISPROVE it. Added 2026-08-08 after the operator overturned owner=NEGATIVE on the dead field: traffic absence proves the carrier dead, not the owner absent.

admission_gates.order_observability: M29 proves the priority is OBSERVABLE: swapping the gates changes what the operator receives when a request trips BOTH. Historical measurement stands: the same swap left 7139 tests green on 2026-08-07; it now reds one test. What M29 does NOT prove — see order_semantics.
admission_gates.order_semantics: UNDER_QUESTION (operator's review 2026-08-08 overturned a claim of mine). The test asserts one direction — domain refusal beats clarification — but the CORRECTNESS of that direction is unproven, and I had no authority to ratify it. History of the overreach: I called it 'operator-endorsed', but the operator had offered that sentence with 'например' (as an EXAMPLE of the invariant's FORM, pin the outcome not the line order), never as ratification of this priority. Two live arguments, neither closed: FOR — a safety stop should beat a usability prompt, because a clarification presupposes eventual compliance the ODD refusal forbids (fail-closed); AGAINST — the ambiguity may mean the ODD detector fired on a misreading, and refusing first suppresses a clarification that would dissolve a false ODD positive. The test stays as a REGRESSION GUARD on the currently-committed order (so a swap is not silent), NOT as proof the order is right. Promotion to PROVEN needs the system owner to ratify the priority as a design decision; until then it is UNDER_QUESTION.

path_ledger._arc_rule: FORMAL, second edition (operator's review 2026-08-08 caught a circularity in the first: if dependence had to be PROVEN for the arc to exist, an unproven nerve could hide behind 'no dependence established, so no arc yet'). EXISTENCE and STATUS are separate questions. A CANDIDATE ARC exists wherever a value actually crosses a phase or module boundary and enters a consumer — no proof of effect required; entering the queue is what makes the effect investigable. STATUS then grades the proof: UNPROVEN — dependence not yet shown; PARTIAL — part of the causal chain proven (e.g. delivery yes, effect mock-blind: the prompt_to_model family is PARTIAL by construction); PROVEN — dependence + semantics + protection shown; DEAD — absence of causal effect proven. An arc ends at the last consumer provable without a live model; hops into a live model form their own PARTIAL arcs. Granularity notes may group physical sites; they never delete a candidate. CLAUSE SHARPENED 2026-08-08 after the operator made me defend turn_context_read: a granularity note may group ONLY the physical sites of the SAME value -> SAME consumer-contract pair (several call sites delivering one routed model to one planner contract, say). Different VALUES or different CONSUMERS are different candidate arcs however tidy it would be to group them — the rule needed no weakening, it had been violated: one record had held prompt blocks, a suppression flag and a durable stats write under a single CERTIFIED verdict, and one of those consumers had never been tested. goal -> retrieval (C15) is the standing example of the other half of the rule: a candidate arc held as UNPROVEN precisely because its dependence is not yet shown.
path_ledger._mandate: Operator mandate 2026-08-08: dissect, prove and certify the whole CNS runtime control path. Clusters follow the REAL execution graph from runtime entry points, never file order. Statuses from path_statuses; UNPROVEN never becomes an assumption; a call edge is never a proven signal flow. A cluster is closed only when its report (SCOPE -> EXECUTION PATH -> SIGNALS/STATE -> OWNERSHIP -> FAILURE SEMANTICS -> TEST EVIDENCE -> MUTATION EVIDENCE -> VERDICT -> NEXT EDGE) exists and its critical contracts have proven bites. This ledger is the work queue and the proof journal, not the goal.
